# Provenance of the `web` module's fixtures

Every file in this directory is written by hand for the tests in
`tests/test_web.py`. None is a capture of a live site or of a live provider
answer: each follows the shape public documentation describes, named below,
and holds only invented text.

| File | Shape it follows | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page_basic.html` | WHATWG HTML Living Standard — §13.2 *Parsing HTML documents* (raw-text `script`/`style` elements, comments, named and numeric character references: <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html>) and §4.2.2 *The `title` element* (<https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-title-element>). A `<title>`, a `<style>`, a `<script>` of more than 5 KiB, a comment, `&eacute;` and `&#x263A;`, and three `<p>` blocks; each skipped part plants a `*_SENTINEL` string the tests assert is absent. | AC7 (P3) |
| `page_latin1.html` | WHATWG HTML Living Standard — §13.2.3 *The input byte stream*, the encoding sniffing algorithm: the transport-layer `charset` first, then the `<meta charset>` prescan of the first 1024 bytes (<https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#the-input-byte-stream>), and the WHATWG Encoding Standard's labels (<https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#names-and-labels>). ISO-8859-1 bytes (`0xE9` for `é`, `0xE8` for `è`) under `<meta charset="iso-8859-1">`. | AC7 (P3) |
| `page_20k.html` | WHATWG HTML Living Standard — §4.4.1 *The `p` element* (<https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-p-element>), §4.2.5 *The `meta` element* `charset` declaration (<https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-meta-charset>) and §4.2.2 *The `title` element*. A UTF-8 document whose extracted text is exactly 20 000 bytes of invented French sentences with two- and three-byte characters (`é`, `☺`, `—`), laid out so that byte 8192 of the text falls inside a multi-byte character; a `<style>` that never reaches the text. | AC8 (P5) |
| `mediawiki_search_8.json` | MediaWiki Action API — `list=search` (*API:Search*, <https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Search>), with `srprop=snippet` and `formatversion=2` (*API:JSON version 2*, <https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:JSON_version_2>): `batchcomplete`, `continue.sroffset`, `query.searchinfo.totalhits` and `query.search[]` of `ns`, `title`, `pageid` and `snippet`. Eight invented results whose snippets carry `<span class="searchmatch">` markup and `&amp;`; the third snippet's extracted text has byte 50 inside the two-byte `é`; the second title is `Café (film)`. | AC5, AC18 (P6) |
| `mediawiki_search_empty.json` | The same documentation: a well-formed answer with `query.searchinfo.totalhits: 0` and an empty `query.search` list. | AC18 (P6) |
| `brave_web_search_3.json` | Brave Search API — *Web Search* response model (`WebSearchApiResponse`, `Search`, `SearchResult`: <https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/app/documentation/web-search/responses>) and the endpoint `GET /res/v1/web/search` (<https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/app/documentation/web-search/get-started>): `type`, `query`, `mixed` and `web.results[]` of `title`, `url`, `description` (with `<strong>` markup), `profile`, `meta_url` and the other documented fields. Three invented results, the second with no `url`. | AC6 (P6) |
| `brave_web_search_no_results.json` | The same documentation: a response with `type`, `query` and an empty `mixed`, and no `web` object — as Brave answers some empty searches; the specification classifies it as malformed. | AC6 (P6) |
